cases.customer_question: Does changing a BLE service UUID from a SIG-defined 16-bit UUID to a custom 128-bit UUID require Bluetooth SIG qualification update or declaration changes?
question_variants: Do custom 128-bit UUIDs affect SIG qualification?
Is SIG update required after changing service UUIDs?
Does switching from standard UUID to custom UUID require requalification?
Are custom GATT services declared in SIG registration?
Do we need new testing for a custom 128-bit UUID?
cases.actual_issue: The customer planned to replace a SIG-defined 16-bit BLE service UUID with a proprietary 128-bit UUID and needed to know whether the change affected Bluetooth SIG qualification or required declaration updates.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The product originally used standard Bluetooth SIG service UUIDs, but the company wanted to switch to its own custom service UUIDs. The consultant explained that custom 128-bit UUID services are treated as proprietary profiles outside the SIG-defined profile test specifications. Because the SIG does not explicitly manage or validate these proprietary profile definitions, no qualification update or additional declaration was required.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant explained that LE profiles using proprietary 128-bit UUIDs are treated as custom profiles and are not tied to SIG-defined Test Specifications or PTS coverage. Because these custom profiles are outside the formal SIG qualification definition scope, the SIG does not require explicit declaration of the proprietary profile implementation or upload of related test reports. Validation responsibility remains with the implementing manufacturer. Therefore, no qualification change application or additional SIG action was required.
cases.decision_logic: Bluetooth SIG qualification formally validates SIG-defined profiles and specifications. Proprietary 128-bit UUID services outside SIG-defined profile specifications are not explicitly declared or validated through standard SIG profile qualification workflows.
cases.final_recommendation: Implement the proprietary 128-bit UUID service as a custom profile without updating the SIG declaration, while internally validating interoperability and functionality at the manufacturer level.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Misunderstanding the qualification scope may lead to unnecessary requalification work, unnecessary test effort, or confusion about declaration obligations for proprietary GATT services.
